source.name: nflverse
source.changes: Play-by-play was summed into team rates for each game. Those rates were turned into team strength and the Coach's Line. Odds Edge is not affiliated with nflverse.

backtest.method: Walk-forward by week. Each week is scored by a model trained only on earlier weeks. Same-week games are not used. The split is not random.
backtest.stake: 1.10 staked to win 1.00, the usual -110 price

flagged.rule: Bet only when our number and the closing number differ by 2.5 points or more.

backtest.plainEnglish: Tested on 2885 regular-season games from 2015–2026, one week at a time, using only earlier weeks to train. Betting the side our number liked, at the closing spread, at the usual -110 price: it hit 50.8% (1428 wins, 1382 losses, 75 pushes). Profit was -2.9% of the money staked. That is not an edge. A -110 bet needs about 52.4% just to break even, and these past weeks did not clear that bar. The Coach's Line is still shown so you can compare it with the books. It is not a pick. Our number was closer to the final margin than the closing number in 42.4% of these games (average miss 10.4 points for us, 9.8 points for the close). That is not a bettor's closing-line value, because the historical file only has the closing number, not the number from earlier in the week. On the smaller slice where our number and the close differed by at least 2.5 points (1399 decided games): hit 50.7%, profit -3.2% of the stake. A smaller slice is easier to overread. The same style of test on totals, betting over or under at -110, hit 49.3% and returned -5.8% of the stake.

backtest.method: Walk-forward by week. The line starts at the closing number. Scales and the recalibration use only earlier weeks. Same-week games are not used.
backtest.stake: 1.10 staked to win 1.00, the usual -110 price

flagged.rule: The side version 2 liked, only when its number and the close differed by 2.5 points or more.

backtest.plainEnglish: Version 2 was tested on 2885 regular-season games from 2015–2026, one week at a time. The number starts at the closing line. Only earlier weeks can move it, and only for a quarterback change, outs weighted by snaps, weather on an open roof, and rest or travel. Betting the side it liked, at the closing spread, at the usual -110 price: it hit 50.5% (1418 wins, 1392 losses, 75 pushes). Profit was -3.6% of the money staked. Brier 0.250. Log loss 0.694. That is not an edge against the market. A -110 bet needs about 52.4% to break even. It was closer to the final margin than the close in 46.8% of these games (average miss 9.8 points, the close 9.8). Moving off the market did not help on the past slice where the number differed, so the games do not say it differs from the books. Version 2 is the number on the game cards because its chances were closer to what happened than version 1. The same test on totals hit 53.0% and returned 1.1% of the stake. That is not an edge on totals either.
